question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: An elective termination performed using modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.C: A legal surgical procedure performed by a certified gynecologist
options.D: A termination done without proper medical training or in unsterile settings

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means it was carried out by untrained hands or in dirty places, which puts the patient at a huge risk for severe complications. Spotting this definition helps you protect your patients early!

question: Why do many women end up turning to dangerous, clandestine abortion methods?

options.A: A personal preference for traditional herbal treatments over hospitals
options.B: Mandatory government programs requiring family planning compliance
options.C: Restrictive laws, social stigma, and poor access to contraception
options.D: Abundant availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas

explanation: It's all about barriers! When society judges harshly and legal or financial access to safe care is blocked, desperate situations drive people toward risky alternatives. Understanding this helps us practice with empathy, not judgment.

question: What is the most common and immediate cause of death after an unsafe abortion?
explanation: Heavy, uncontrolled bleeding is the number one emergency here. When tissues are torn or left behind in unsterile procedures, severe bleeding can turn fatal very quickly if we don't act fast.

question: A patient comes in after a clandestine abortion with a high fever, smelly vaginal discharge, and lower tummy pain. What is the most likely problem?
explanation: Fever plus foul-smelling discharge is a red flag for infection. Unsterile instruments easily introduce bacteria right into the uterus, leading quickly to pelvic sepsis. Great clinical spotting!

question: Why do nurses need to keep a close eye out when caring for women with sudden tummy pain in the emergency ward?

options.A: Patients may hide a history of unsafe abortion due to fear or legal stigma
options.B: Abortion complications never present with abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.C: Routine screening policies forbid nurses from asking about sexual history
options.D: Standard diagnostic tests cannot detect early stages of pregnancy

explanation: Fear of judgment or legal trouble often makes patients keep quiet about what really happened. As nurses, our compassionate detective work helps us uncover the truth and save lives!

question: Which physical sign strongly points toward a uterine perforation or pelvic peritonitis?

options.A: Painless bilateral swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Generalized skin rash and localized itching
options.C: Elevated blood pressure and clear breath sounds
options.D: A rigid and tender abdomen with rebound tenderness

explanation: When the lining of the belly (peritoneum) gets irritated or infected, the abdominal muscles lock up tight ('rigidity'), and pressing and letting go hurts sharply ('rebound tenderness'). A classic exam and ward clue!

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for a patient going into shock from severe post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: Perform a detailed psychosocial history regarding the pregnancy
options.B: Send the patient immediately for diagnostic pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Administer oral rehydration salts and counsel on contraception
options.D: Insert large-bore intravenous lines for fluid resuscitation

explanation: ABC comes first—and in bleeding shock, getting IV lines open fast to pump fluids and restore blood volume is an absolute lifesaver! You've got this.

question: Aside from giving fluids, what type of medication is routinely given right away if an infected (septic) abortion is suspected?
explanation: Infection spreads fast! Starting broad-spectrum IV antibiotics early stops bacteria in their tracks and prevents the patient from sliding into full septic shock.

question: What are the main parts of Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, blood donation drives, and psychiatric isolation
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkages
options.C: Mandatory legal reporting, punitive counseling, and moral interrogation
options.D: Routine hysterectomy, genetic testing, and long-term foster care referral

explanation: PAC is a complete care package: treat the immediate danger, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect them to healthy support networks. Brilliant concept to master!

question: What is the main goal of "value clarification" workshops for nursing staff?

options.A: To train nurses on advanced surgical procedures like abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: To enforce strict legal penalties against patients who induce abortions
options.C: To help nurses set aside personal biases to provide non-judgmental care
options.D: To update hospital billing policies for emergency obstetric services

explanation: We all have personal beliefs, but value clarification helps us check our biases at the door so we can treat every single patient with professional, loving kindness.

question: How does making modern contraception easy for everyone to get help lower maternal death rates?

options.A: By shortening the normal physiological gestation period for women
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for emergency obstetric departments
options.C: By preventing all forms of sexually transmitted bacterial infections
options.D: By reducing the incidence of unintended pregnancies and unsafe abortions

explanation: Prevention is key! When people can easily access contraception, unplanned pregnancies drop, which means fewer people resort to dangerous, life-threatening unsafe abortions.

question: Which healthcare approach works best when teaching young people about reproductive health?

options.A: Mandatory public announcements broadcast only in corporate workplaces
options.B: Strict punitive laws targeting teenagers seeking health information
options.C: Youth-friendly clinics offering confidential counseling and contraceptives
options.D: Excluding adolescents from family planning discussions until marriage

explanation: Young people want privacy and a welcoming environment without fear of being scolded. Youth-friendly clinics build trust so teens actually feel safe seeking help!
